The song was the second single from the album, released in both the UK and international territories. You Don't Love Me (Willie Cobbs song) | "You Don't Love Me" is a rhythm and blues-influenced blues song recorded by American musician Willie Cobbs in 1960.  It is Cobbs' best-known song and features a guitar figure and melody that has appealed to musicians in several genres.  Although it became a regional hit when it was released in Memphis, Tennessee, copyright issues prevented its further promotion and national chart success.  Derived from an earlier song by Bo Diddley, it has inspired many popular adaptations, including "Shimmy Shimmy Walk" by the Megatons and "You Don't Love Me (No, No, No)" by Jamaican singer Dawn Penn.
